newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices seen rising as demand picks up.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices seen rising as demand picks up.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to rise further this week before succumbing to profit taking due to tight supplies from the Philippines and Indonesia, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"Poor shipments from the Philippines will keep prices at current high levels," said one trader.
Additional shipments from Indonesia will not be enough to meet rising demand, Manila traders said.

"Coconut oil prices generally hit the roof last week due to delayed shipments from the Philippines and speculation that typhoon Dale might hit coconut growing areas in the Bicol region (in the central Philippines)," traders said.
Prices of coconut oil in storage at Rotterdam were quoted at a premium of between $75 and $80 per tonne CIF last week above prices of coconut oil en route to Europe, one trader said.
The trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines said coconut oil prices soared to an average price of $771 CIF per tonne last week as against $731.25 the previous week.

One Manila trader said coconut oil prices for October/November shipments hit a high of $830 per tonne CIF last week. "Prices pulled back to $800 CIF per tonne at the close last week from $747.20 CIF per tonne at the start," he said.
Traders said prices have been further boosted by delayed shipments of coconut oil from the Philippines in the past several weeks due to fewer ships carrying the commodity to Europe and United States.
"Before, two or more vessels shipped coconut oil per destination. Now, only one vessel carries the commodity per destination due to poor supply from the Philippines," said one trader.

The independent Oil World newsletter reported last week that expectations of lower Philippine coconut oil output had brought stock drawdowns in the United States, Europe and other importing countries.
"Prices have hit high levels. I expect profit taking anytime this week," a trader in a major coconut oil mill told Reuters.

But two other vegetable oil traders said commercial buyers were still adamant against releasing their stocks on expectations that prices would rise further due to increasing demand for the Christmas holidays.
"Prices still have an upside at the start of this week. But prices cannot go on hitting the roof forever. Some will take profits at the right price," said one trader.
